heroHeadline: Day 597: DHS Secretary Mullin in Mexico City for Bilateral Security Talks; Anti-Narco Electoral Reform Sent to Congress; EU-Mexico Summit Tomorrow
heroSubtitle: On May 20–21, 2026 (Days 596–597), five major developments defined the mid-week agenda. MEXICO PEACE INDEX (MAY 20): The IEP released the Mexico Peace Index 2026, recording a 5.1% peace improvement — the biggest annual gain in over a decade and the sixth consecutive year of improvement. Total homicides fell 22.7% (approx. 7,000 fewer deaths than 2024), the largest single-year absolute decline on record. Sheinbaum highlighted the data as validation of her security strategy. Ongoing structural risks noted: rising disappearances, extortion, and domestic violence. RAIL MEGA-PLAN (MAY 20): The federal government announced plans to build 2,377 km of new passenger and cargo railway lines, including Mexico City–Pachuca, Mexico City–Querétaro, Querétaro–Irapuato, and Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo corridors, plus a Tren Maya cargo extension and infrastructure across 2,300 municipalities — a signature infrastructural diversification play ahead of USMCA review. PRECIO JUSTO CORN AGREEMENT (MAY 20): Sheinbaum signed the 'Precio Justo' white corn accord covering 61,000 producers, 705,000 hectares, and 7M tons annually, with major corn flour mills (80% of formal sector) committing to stabilize producer and consumer prices amid international corn prices up 50%. García Harfuch also confirmed Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya has lost Guardia Nacional protection — state police now cover him exclusively. DHS SECRETARY MULLIN BILATERAL VISIT (MAY 21): U.S. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin (confirmed March 2026, replacing Kristi Noem) arrived in Mexico City at 12:00 hrs for his first official bilateral security meeting with García Harfuch and Mexico's Security Cabinet — part of the diplomatic framework agreed in the May 16 Trump-Sheinbaum phone call ahead of U.S. envoy visits (~May 27) and the first USMCA bilateral round (week of May 25). Drug czar Sara Carter's accompanying visit was postponed to May 25. Sheinbaum reiterated the sovereignty-plus-cooperation framing. ANTI-NARCO ELECTORAL REFORM (MAY 21): Sheinbaum sent to Congress an initiative creating an INE Commission for Verification of Integrity of Candidacies — a body that would consult intelligence agencies to screen 2027 midterm candidacies for organized crime ties. Targeting 'narco-candidacies' after the Rocha Moya DOJ indictment and Operation Enjambre arrests. EU-MEXICO SUMMIT (MAY 22, TOMORROW): The historic 8th EU-Mexico Summit — first in 11 years — is tomorrow in Mexico City, where EU Council President Costa and Commission President von der Leyen will sign the Modernised Global Agreement and Interim Trade Agreement (approved by all 27 EU states May 11), projected to boost bilateral commerce by ~35% and materially strengthen Mexico's USMCA negotiating hand.
